name: The LLM Surgeon
problem: Data-driven compression of pretrained LLMs usually treats pruning and weight-update as separate problems, and unstructured pruning of a large model was thought to need full second-order computation.
mechanism: Scales Kronecker-FACTORIZED curvature approximations (KFAC) of the target loss landscape to LLM scale, which is what makes it affordable, and uses them to do two coupled things at once: dynamically allocate which structures can be removed, AND update the surviving weights to account for the removal. The weight-update term is improved to capture more correlations between weights than prior second-order methods. Unifies unstructured, semi-structured and structured pruning in one framework.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): prunes ROWS AND COLUMNS from a range of OPT models and LLaMA2-7B BY 20%-30% with 'a negligible loss in performance', and achieves state-of-the-art results in unstructured and semi-structured pruning of LLMs. COMPRESSION RATIO: 20-30% structural removal (1.25x-1.43x), and higher when unstructured. QUALITY COST: 'negligible loss in performance' with no paired number in the abstract. Note the tension with the training-free methods above: LLM Surgeon DOES update weights, which is where its quality comes from and what makes it slower than Wanda.
